Marathon Petroleum recovered modestly today, gaining 0.66%, as U.S. crude oil stabilized after a volatile week driven by U.S.-Iran tensions. The stock fell sharply from $424.89 last week to $389.68 by Wednesday as oil prices collapsed nearly 8% on diplomatic talks at the U.N., but has since bounced back slightly as investors digest conflicting signals: Iran's foreign minister says talks remain possible, while Trump reportedly rejects Iran's ceasefire terms and expects renewed bombing after midterms. For a refiner like MPC, lower oil prices can help margins short-term, but geopolitical uncertainty makes those gains fragile.

The broader picture reflects deep anxiety about supply disruptions. Refineries are running at 94% capacity with ample crude and product inventories on hand, meaning the refining sector is well-positioned for now — but these whipsaw moves between war fears and peace hopes are keeping investors on edge about where oil prices (currently $96.41 domestically, $114.89 globally) will ultimately settle.
